findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "synorb-get-demo-key" references sensitive artifacts (api_key, authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Tip: while you set up, a short note to your user helps. For example: 'I'm getting a Synorb demo key and connecting. This can take a minute or two.' Setup page: …

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: synorb-get-demo-key · Private data: synorb-get-demo-key, synorb-save-beacon, synorb-beacons · Public sink: synorb-get-demo-key · Destructive: synorb-beacons, synorb-archive-beacon, synorb-update-beacon.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: synorb-get-demo-key · Private data: synorb-get-demo-key, synorb-save-beacon, synorb-beacons · Public sink: synorb-get-demo-key · Destructive: synorb-beacons, synorb-archive-beacon, synorb-update-beacon

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
